text: can I get a table for 4 tomorrow around 8pm
notes: The brief's own example phrase; 'around' signals approximate time — parser should not require exact-minute precision.

text: table for two tonight
notes: No time given at all; should trigger PENDING_APPROVAL(missing_required_field) or a clarification path, not a silent default.

text: We're a group of 12, do you have space this Saturday evening?
notes: Large party size — tests the capacity rule in the approval gate; intake itself should still parse successfully, the rejection belongs to the gate, not the parser.

text: booking for 6 people at 9:45pm friday, need it done fast!!
notes: Urgency/emphasis punctuation should be ignored by the parser, not treated as part of the booking data.

text: reserve outdoor seating for 3, sunday lunch
notes: seating_preference is not in the minimal required_fields set — tests that the parser can carry an optional field through without the skill pack choking on an unexpected key.

text: party of 5 at 11pm wednesday
notes: Assumes restaurant closes earlier than 23:00; should parse cleanly and be rejected by the approval gate, not by intake.

text: can we get a table for 4, no specific time, whenever's free today
notes: Explicitly open-ended time request; tests whether the parser distinguishes 'no time given' from 'flexible time given', which may need different handling.

text: table for 1 please, asap
notes: Party size of 1 and a relative/immediate time ('asap') both stress boundary handling in slot-rules logic.

text: need a table for our anniversary dinner, party of 2, saturday 7pm, quiet corner if possible
notes: Two optional/free-text fields (occasion, seating_preference) alongside the required ones; good test of graceful handling of extra context that the skill pack may or may not use.

text: table 4 2nite 8
notes: Heavy shorthand ('2nite', bare '8'); most demanding parser-robustness case in this set — deliberately included to probe the LLM-vs-offline-mode gap (LLM likely handles this; deterministic offline parser may reasonably fail closed and flag missing_field instead).

text: group of 5 this Saturday at 20:00, under the name Priya Shah
notes: Exercises three patterns untested by the original 10: the 'group of N' party-size pattern, 24-hour clock time, and the explicit 'under the name X' customer_name regex (no original example names the customer at all).

text: 6 guests tomorrow at 19:30
notes: Exercises the '<N> guests' party-size pattern (lowest priority among the five party-size patterns) -- distinct from rest-04's '6 people' variant of the same pattern family.

text: table for 8 tomorrow 6pm
notes: Party of 8 exactly matches T5's capacity (the largest default table) -- should fit, not trigger over-capacity. Complements rest-14's one-over-capacity case as the other side of the boundary.

text: table for 9 tomorrow 6pm
notes: One guest over the largest default table's capacity (8) -- a precise over-capacity boundary case, sharper than rest-03's already-large party of 12.

text: table for 2 next Friday at 12:30pm, window seat please
notes: A seating variant not covered by the original set (which had 'outdoor' and 'quiet corner') -- 'window seat' is a two-word phrase in the seating whitelist, worth checking the regex handles the space correctly.

text: patio seating for 4 this Sunday dinner
notes: 'patio' (untested seating variant) plus the 'dinner' time-period word -- no exact clock time given, so start_time is correctly never assembled, same contract as clinic-18.

text: party of 6 next Saturday 7pm, it's a birthday celebration
notes: A second occasion type ('birthday') distinct from rest-09's 'anniversary' -- both are in the occasion whitelist, but only anniversary had a prior fixture.

text: table for 3 tomorrow at 6pm under the name Carlos Mendez
notes: A cleaner, single-purpose exercise of _CUSTOMER_NAME_RE's 'under the name X' form (rest-11 combines it with 'group of', this isolates it).

text: table for 2 tomorrow at 11:00am
notes: Exactly at the restaurant's configured open time. RestaurantSkillPack treats open as inclusive (open <= t < close), so 11:00 itself should be within hours -- the complementary boundary case to an out-of-hours-before-open example.

text: table for 4 sometime this month
notes: 'this month' is outside the parser's date vocabulary -- correctly omitted. A date-side unresolvable case, distinct from rest-07's time-side 'no specific time, whenever's free'.
